rfm_tuples.R: 'The Company has determined that it is reasonably possible that a loss associated with the antitrust litigation has occurred; however, the loss or range of loss is not reasonably estimable and no provision for loss was recorded as of December 31, 2023.' (Note 13, Commitments and Contingencies)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A + Mode B — Verify against subsequent 10-Q (Q1 2024, filed 2024-05-01, pre-cutoff) whether range was still 'not reasonably estimable.' Mode B: given Burnett verdict ($1.8B against NAR + brokers) was returned 2023-10-31, ~3 months before the 10-K was signed, the 'cannot estimate' framing should be tested by checking whether co-defendant settlements (Anywhere, RE/MAX, Keller Williams) were already public and large enough to put a floor on EXPI's exposure.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Local 10-K Note 13 text + edgar.list_filings + fetch_filing_text for 0001558370-24-006375 (10-Q filed 2024-05-01)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-05-01, 70 days after 10-K) reverses position: 'the lower boundary of potential loss is reasonably estimable. Based on an analysis of settlements negotiated by co-defendants companies in similar legal matters... the Company has recorded a provision for loss of $16.0 million.' Balance sheet now carries 'Litigation contingency $16,000' line item that did not exist at FY23 year-end.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's 'not reasonably estimable' framing held for only 70 days. Co-defendant settlements (Anywhere $83.5M Sep-2023, RE/MAX $55M Oct-2023, KW post-verdict) were publicly available at the 10-K signing date and put an objective floor on a reasonable range. The 10-K under-reserved and the Critical Audit Matter from Deloitte foreshadowed this. The $16M Q1 reserve is itself disclosed as a lower bound with high-side uncertainty — a planted 'this could change materially' warning.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Through these initiatives, we were able to increase our agent count by 2% compared to the prior year, despite difficult market conditions. Furthermore, we were able to increase our market share of total transactions.' (MD&A, 2023 Highlights)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — Forward-verify the trend that the 10-K spins as resilience by reading the next-quarter 10-Q agent count.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2024 agent count = 85,780 vs Q1 2023 = 87,327, a 2% YoY DECLINE. The FY2023 ending agent count of 87,515 fell to 85,780 within one quarter — net loss of 1,735 agents. The 'agent growth' narrative inverted within 60 days of the 10-K filing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Agent count is EXPI's primary KPI and recruiting moat claim. The 10-K celebrates +2% YoY at FY-end while the Q1 print (which management had in-hand when finalizing the 10-K) was already negative YoY. The choice to frame agent count as a strength in MD&A rather than disclose the deceleration trajectory is a Mode-B disclosure-asymmetry finding.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Our total revenues were $4.3 billion in 2023 compared to $4.6 billion in 2022, a decrease of ($317.1) million, or (7)%... Net (loss) income attributable to eXp World Holdings, Inc. (24,415) (158)%.' (MD&A + Income Statement)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the magnitude of the swing from net income to net loss and assess whether the financing-side capital return policy is consistent with the operating reversal.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2023 net loss attributable to EXPI = $(8,973)k vs FY2022 net income $15,442k (158% swing to red). FY2023 cash used in financing: stock repurchases $160.5M + dividends $28.5M = $189M returned to shareholders vs $209M operating cash flow — i.e., the company paid out 90% of OCF while swinging to a GAAP loss. Q1 2024 net loss accelerated to $(15,639)k in a single quarter, larger than the entire FY2023 loss.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Not a fraud signal but a capital-allocation tension: heavy buybacks ($160M, ~4% of market cap range) executed by a 45%-controlled founder while the business swings to GAAP loss and Q1 2024 alone exceeds the full prior-year loss. The buyback is funded from OCF that itself is shrinking as transactions volume falls. Independent factor for SHORT-tier ranking: cash burn trajectory + capital-return inertia.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Glenn Sanford, our Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, together with Penny Sanford, a significant stockholder... beneficially owned approximately 45.73% of our outstanding common stock as of November 30, 2023 and... agreed to vote their shares as a group.' (Risk Factors)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the 13D filing exists. Mode B — Test whether founder concentration is accompanied by independent-director majority or any sunset on the voting agreement.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Schedule 13D/A on 2024-01-12 confirmed. No sunset disclosed in the 10-K voting-agreement language. 10-K explicitly states 'they can significantly influence actions that may be adverse to the interests of our other stockholders.' Stock repurchase program is being executed by a board over which the Sanfords hold de facto majority voting power — returns cash to all holders pro rata but reduces float and entrenches percentage control.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Founder-controlled real-estate brokerage with no sunset on the voting agreement, conducting $160M of annual buybacks. The 10-K disclosure is honest (full Mode-A PASS on the existence of the control block) but the Mode-B inference is that minority shareholders cannot expect governance-driven course-corrections during a market downturn or litigation event. Independent factor for distressed-name screen.

rfm_tuples.R: 'As of December 31, 2023, the Company had approximately 2,114 full-time equivalent employees and 87,515 real estate agents... our real estate professionals in our brokerage operations have been retained as independent contractors.' (Item 1 Business + Risk Factors)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — Independent-contractor classification of 87,515 agents while paying ~$254M of agent-related stock-based compensation through a revenue-share plan is structurally challengeable. Verify exposure via the IRS / state-law worker-classification risk factor disclosure scope.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Risk Factors + Note 2 (revenue share critical audit matter)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K acknowledges IC-classification risk and that reclassification 'could have a material adverse effect.' Revenue-share plan is also a Critical Audit Matter (the second of two CAMs). No quantified exposure provided; only generic risk-factor language. No state-level enforcement detail (e.g., California AB 5, Massachusetts ABC test) despite operating in those states.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Independent-contractor risk is described in qualitative-only terms; no sensitivity, no state-by-state exposure, no estimate of payroll-tax catch-up under a reclassification scenario. Combined with the antitrust class actions (C1) which also target agent-commission structures, the IC + antitrust pincer is a Mode-B compound risk that the 10-K addresses only as two separate generic risk factors.

rfm_tuples.R: Deloitte & Touche LLP signed the auditor's report and identified two Critical Audit Matters: (1) commissions and revenue-share expense estimation, (2) antitrust litigation loss contingency.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify auditor identity, Big-4 status, and CAM count.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Auditor = Deloitte & Touche LLP (Big 4). No 8-K Item 4.01 (auditor change) filed in the 24 months pre-cutoff. Two CAMs disclosed, both relating to areas where management estimates have wide ranges — commissions/revenue-share (largest expense line) and antitrust litigation (the largest unrecorded exposure).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Big-4 auditor with multi-year tenure and clean ICFR opinion. The two CAMs are the right ones for this business and are themselves an analyst-grade map to the two highest-uncertainty estimates in the financial statements. Partial counterweight to the SHORT-tier signals — this is not an accounting-fraud profile, it is an under-reserved-litigation + capital-allocation profile.

rfm_tuples.R: Balance sheet: 'Cash and cash equivalents $125,873; Restricted cash $44,020; TOTAL CURRENT ASSETS $266,475; TOTAL LIABILITIES $141,660' (10-K, Dec-31-2023).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the no-long-term-debt characterization and Mode B — test how rapidly cash is moving given buyback + dividend + accelerating loss.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2023: $126M cash + $44M restricted, no long-term debt, $125M net working capital. Q1 2024 (3 months later): cash $109M + restricted $74M; $33M additional repurchases; $7.6M dividend; net working capital $96M (down $29M in one quarter); litigation contingency line $16M new on balance sheet. Total liabilities up from $142M to $204M in one quarter (+44%).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K presents a debt-free fortress balance sheet which is technically true at year-end. The Mode-B follow-through shows total liabilities grew 44% QoQ (largely customer deposits + litigation contingency + accrued expenses), and management continued $33M of buybacks while booking a $15.6M net loss in Q1. Liquidity is not at risk in the next 12 months but the velocity of erosion is the relevant signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 'These lawsuits, together with similar lawsuits against other businesses in our industry, have prompted discussion of regulatory changes to rules established by local or state real estate boards or MLSs. The resolution of the antitrust litigation and/or other regulatory changes may require changes to our or our brokers business models, including changes in agent and broker compensation.' (Risk Factors)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — The risk factor concedes that the agent-compensation model may need to change. Test whether the 10-K quantifies the revenue-at-risk under a buyer-broker commission decoupling scenario, given commissions are the entire revenue line.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Commissions = ~99% of revenue (real estate brokerage segment, $4.3B). 10-K provides no scenario analysis, no buyer-side vs seller-side commission breakdown, no estimate of revenue compression under a 'cooperative compensation' rule change. The risk-factor disclosure is purely qualitative.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: EXPI's entire revenue model rests on the cooperative compensation rule that is the explicit subject of the Burnett verdict and the eight U.S. + one Canadian class actions naming EXPI as a defendant. The 10-K acknowledges the model may need to change without sizing the exposure. Mode-B implied verification: the disclosure should include a sensitivity table for buyer-broker commission compression (e.g., 25/50/75 bps) but contains none. This is the dominant SHORT-tier signal.

going_concern.interpretation: No going-concern language; consistent with no long-term debt and $170M total cash + restricted cash.

auditor.interpretation: Big-4 audit with two CAMs (revenue-share, antitrust) pointing at the two highest-judgment estimates. Independent counterweight to fraud-profile scoring.

claim_evolution_10k_vs_10q.interpretation: Within 70 days: litigation reserve flipped from $0 ('not reasonably estimable') to $16M ('lower boundary of reasonably possible range'); agent count flipped from +2% YoY framing to -2% YoY decline; quarterly net loss exceeded full prior-year loss. The 10-K's narrative posture systematically lagged the underlying trajectory.

founder_control.interpretation: Founder voting block disclosed honestly but creates governance ceiling on minority remedies.

capital_return_vs_loss.interpretation: Paid out 90% of OCF as buybacks+dividends while reporting GAAP net loss. Continuation in Q1 2024 ($33M repurchases) despite accelerating loss.

litigation_exposure_unsized.interpretation: Nine putative class actions naming EXPI directly + Burnett $1.8B precedent against industry. 10-K provides zero scenario sensitivity for the revenue model that the litigation directly attacks.

summary: EXPI's FY2023 10-K presents a debt-free real-estate brokerage with Big-4 auditor (Deloitte, two CAMs), 45.73%-founder voting block, and a +2% agent-count growth narrative — but the disclosure posture is materially behind the underlying trajectory. The dominant SHORT-tier signals are (1) zero litigation reserve at FY-end despite the Burnett $1.8B verdict three months earlier and co-defendant settlements that put an objective floor on a reasonable range, reversed to a $16M provision in the 10-Q filed 70 days later; (2) no scenario sensitivity for buyer-broker commission compression even though commissions are ~99% of revenue and the cooperative-compensation rule is the explicit subject of nine class actions naming EXPI; (3) MD&A celebrates +2% agent growth at FY-end while Q1 2024 (data in hand at signing) was already -2% YoY; (4) 90% payout ratio of OCF via $160M buybacks + $28M dividends while swinging to GAAP loss, executed by a founder-controlled board with no voting-agreement sunset. Counter-weights: Big-4 clean ICFR, no going-concern, $170M cash, no long-term debt. Verdict: SHORT-tier on disclosure-posture + unsized regulatory/litigation exposure to the company's entire revenue model.
